A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same iQUEST research. Text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and complete; pagination differences do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original iQUEST benchmark results and ablations in Section 5 and Appendix A, runtime measurements in Appendix B, and error analyses in Appendices D–E.

after.justification: v5 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, runtime measurements, and error analyses in Section 5 and Appendices A–E.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Section 4 retain identical question generation, SPARQL retrieval, GNN-based two-hop exploration, relevance scoring, answer extraction, and stopping procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use CWQ, WebQSP, WebQuestions, and GrailQA over Freebase. The one-, two-, and three-hop runtime scenarios and missing-knowledge cases are also retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same six comparison methods, including ToG, Interactive-KBQA, KG-CoT, and FlexKBQA. Appendix B still compares against ToG, and all ablation model combinations match.

E3.justification: Both retain Hit@1, the same model configurations, top-three entity retrieval, and 1,000-instance GrailQA sampling. Appendix B retains GPT-4o via Azure OpenAI, 100 questions per hop category, and the correct-chain control.

E4.justification: The KG, IQG-LLM, AE-LLM, and GNN ablations are unchanged. Appendix runtime controls, missing-entity analysis, and the Forrest Gump failure case are retained without additional analyses.

E5.justification: Both report point estimates and average runtimes without repeated-run counts, seed details, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. Uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–9 and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 1 retains iQUEST scores of 73.85, 88.93, 81.23, and 73.52 across the four datasets; relocated appendix tables contain identical values.

T1.justification: The knowledge-graph and task definitions in Section 3 and Equations 1–5 are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about iterative question guidance, two-hop GNN exploration, and effectiveness across four datasets and four LLMs.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning reasoning versus internal knowledge remain identical. Both retain limitations concerning computational overhead, two-hop context, incomplete knowledge graphs, and repetitive or drifting sub-questions.

D1.justification: v5 adds a public-code statement and an iQUEST repository link in the abstract, absent from v4. Other implementation details are unchanged. This establishes new access information; repository contents cannot be assessed from the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning in Section 2 and the introduction are unchanged, including distinctions from question decomposition and one-hop entity exploration.

P1.justification: The title gains the prefix 'iQUEST:' and the abstract gains a code-availability sentence. The remaining prose and section order, including Appendices A–E, are unchanged.

P2.justification: Reflow relocates existing tables: Table 6 moves from PDF page 11 to 12, and Table 8 from page 12 to 13. Appendix E extends onto a sparse page 14. Figures, captions, and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added repository link provides an implementation reference absent from v4, modestly improving access documentation. Scientific content and evidence remain unchanged. More fragmented appendix pagination is a small presentation drawback, but the documented access benefit supports a limited net improvement.
